messages:
Sam: Heads-up — we started getting a support escalation from a customer in EU about latency. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~320ms, p99 from ~240ms to ~980ms around 09:12 UTC. Error rates are low but latency complaints on hosted API /v1/chat.

Sam: Customer provided example request ids: req_eu_01a2, req_eu_01b7. They see extra ~150-600ms before first byte sometimes.

Nora: I'm seeing the same in our monitoring — per-route p95 spiked and correlates with eu-west edge pool. Timeline: deploys earlier today were for edge routing tweak (preview) at 08:50 UTC.

Aj: Can we confirm whether this is TLS handshake time or server processing? Graphs show a bump in 'connect_time' vs 'ttfb'.

Devon: Initial traces from the backend show processing unchanged. The big delta is upstream connect/TLS.

Maria: I'll run a traceroute/mtr from the problematic PoP to the backend IPs. Also we should check any recent BGP/edge routing changes.

Maria: Ran mtr for one of the request flows, here's truncated output:
```
Start: eu-w-03 -> backend-eu-01 (10.32.x.x)
 1. 10.32.1.1   0.9ms
 2. 10.32.5.2   1.1ms
 3. 198.51.100.5 45.2ms  (cross-zone hop)
 4. 198.51.200.9  220ms  (another cross-region transit)
 5. backend-eu-01  2.3ms
```
Maria: Notice a strange 200+ms hop in the middle — looks like traffic is being routed through a distant transit node intermittently.

Sam: Customer's tcpdump (they attached) shows repeated full TLS handshakes: not reusing sessions. Some flows show SYN->SYN-ACK delay ~120ms too.

Aj: That suggests connection re-use or TLS session resumption failing at the edge. Any recent cert/server-side changes?

Leo (deploy-bot): deploy edge-routing-preview v3 started at 08:49:12 UTC, 25% traffic.

Kai: I rolled the preview at 25% earlier for canary. Could be a route preference change in the preview that causes some PoPs to favor a backbone with high inter-pop latency.

Maria: Also DNS TTLs: our edge-client DNS resolver TTL is 60s but the preview changed the edge cache policy to 300s for a subset, which can cause stale egress choices.

Devon: To validate, try forcing requests with curl --resolve to bind to specific edge ip and compare timings. Example I ran locally:
```
curl -w "%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer}\n" -o /dev/null -s -v --resolve api.redwood:443:198.51.100.10 https://api.redwood/v1/chat
```
Devon: When resolved to 198.51.100.10 (preferred path), time_connect ~30ms, starttransfer ~70ms. When resolved to 198.51.200.9 (bad path), time_connect ~260ms, starttransfer ~540ms.

Nora: So it's definitely an edge routing path issue — TLS handshake + extra network hops. Might be a routing policy that unintentionally prefers a cheaper/longer backbone route.

Aj: Immediate mitigations we can do now (short list):
- Rollback edge-routing-preview to 0% (stop canary)
- Force DNS cache flush on effected PoPs (lower TTL back to 60s)
- Enable TLS session resumption at edge (if disabled in preview)
- Add a temporary routing rule to prefer local zone egress for eu-west

Maria: I'm going to push a config change to edge routing to revert the preview (canary->0). Pushing now.

Leo (deploy-bot): revert edge-routing-preview v3 -> v2 initiated at 09:28:43 UTC by Maria.

Maria: Also flushing edge DNS caches for eu-west PoPs. Doing a rolling flush (one PoP at a time).

Sam: I pinged customer and asked them to retry a few requests after ~5 minutes. They reported p95 dropped back closer to baseline after ~10m but occasional spikes remain.

Aj: Remaining spikes could be TLS session reuse failures — check handshake metrics (tls_full_handshake_count).

Devon: I pulled metrics: tls_full_handshake_count spiked x3 for eu-west around the same timestamp. Session ticket creation rate also dropped for that canary. Looks like preview altered TLS config for an edge subset.

Kai: We have a mismatch in cipher list ordering in preview — some clients/servers couldn't do session resumption consistently, forcing full handshake. Rolling the config back should fix it.

Maria: To block similar incidents:
- Add a pre-deploy perf test that measures connect_time and handshake rates for any edge routing or TLS config changes.
- Canary traffic should be pinned to a single PoP when testing routing changes to avoid cross-zone effects.
- Add automated alert for sudden increase in cross-pop traceroute latency (we can compute delta > 100ms).

Nora: Also docs/Runbook additions: include quick commands for SRE to triage network vs backend: mtr -c 50, dig +trace, curl --resolve, openssl s_client -msg -connect, and tcpdump filter for TLS handshake "tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0".

Sam: Customer updated: they saw improved latency after the rollback and DNS flush; very grateful. They asked what happened and what we changed.

Aj: Summary for customer (I'll draft): root cause: canary edge-routing change caused intermittent routing through a high-latency transit node and a TLS config mismatch forced full handshakes for some flows. Mitigations: rolled back canary, flushed edge DNS caches, re-enabled TLS session resumption, and pinned canary to a single PoP for future tests. Follow-ups: add pre-deploy perf tests and routing alerts.

Devon: Action items assigned:
- Maria: confirm all PoPs back to normal and push hotfix to prevent preview from toggling TLS ciphers (done)
- Kai: add DNS TTL rollback automation + cache flush runbook (in progress)
- Aj: create alert for handshake spike and cross-pop latency (in progress)
- Sam/Nora: send debrief to customer and attach repro steps we used

Maria: PoPs look stable. Will keep monitoring for 2 hours.

Sam: Closing loop with customer now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Aj: We'll log a postmortem template in incidents/ if spikes resurface.

net-bot: incident ticket #INC-2026-118 created for p95 regression — assigned to eng-sre.

Sam: Saved commands for runbook (copy below):
```
# check DNS path
dig +short @<edge-dns> api.redwood A
# force resolve and check timings
curl -w "%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer}\n" -o /dev/null -s --resolve api.redwood:443:<edge_ip> https://api.redwood/v1/chat
# TLS handshake debug
openssl s_client -connect <edge_ip>:443 -servername api.redwood -msg -tlsextdebug
# traceroute/mtr
mtr -r -c 50 <edge_ip>
# tcpdump filter TLS handshake
tcpdump -nni eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & tcp-syn != 0' and host <edge_ip>
```

Sam: Thread note: keep this Slack thread as the canonical triage notes for the customer issue.

Maria: filing the follow-up items in the backlog.

Leo (deploy-bot): canary rollback completed across eu-west at 09:31:12 UTC.

Sam: thanks everyone, marking thread resolved for now.
